title: Tamil Nadu: Madurai, Thanjavur, Kanchipuram, Mamallapuram, Ooty, Kodaikanal, Rameswaram and Kanyakumari
selection: VacayOut had Chennai and Mamallapuram for Tamil Nadu. This pack adds the state's other main destinations — the temple cities of Madurai, Thanjavur and Kanchipuram, the hill stations of Ooty and Kodaikanal, and Rameswaram and Kanyakumari — with their main sights, things to do, itineraries and guides, researched from Tamil Nadu Tourism (Government of Tamil Nadu) and Wikipedia.

overview.text:
Madurai is called Thoonga Nagaram — 'the city that never sleeps'. References to it go back to the 3rd century BC, and it was a seat of Tamil learning where the Sangam of scholars met; it appears in the Sangam epic Silapathigaram.

The city grew around the Meenakshi Amman Temple, whose 14 towers and thousand-pillared hall still dominate the old centre. Nearby are the 17th-century Thirumalai Nayakar Mahal, the Gandhi Memorial Museum in Rani Mangammal's palace, and the vast Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam, venue of the float festival.

items.body: The Meenakshi Amman Temple's 14 towers and musical pillars.

The Gandhi Memorial Museum, with the cloth Gandhi wore on the day he was killed.

Jain and Hindu monuments on the Samanar hills.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Madurai airport has flights to Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi, and to Colombo, Dubai and Singapore.

By train: Madurai Junction is the main station.

By bus: Mattuthavani (M.G.R.) and Arappalayam handle intercity buses; Periyar bus stand serves the city.

best_time.text: Madurai can be visited year-round, but December to February is the most comfortable. Plan around the festivals: the Chithirai Brahmotsavam with the divine wedding, Navarathri in September–October, and the float festival at the Teppakulam in January–February.

overview.text:
Madurai is synonymous with the Meenakshi Amman Temple. Destroyed in 1310, it was restored in the 14th century and now has 14 towers between 45 and 50 metres tall.

Inside is a thousand-pillared hall of sculpted pillars — some musical, ringing at different notes — a large sacred tank, and corridor murals telling stories from the Thiruvilaiyadal puranam.

overview.text:
Thanjavur is a city of temples, rice fields and the famous Thanjavur paintings. Cholas, Pandyas, Nayaks, Vijayanagara kings and Marathas ruled here in turn, and each left its mark.

The Brihadeeswara Temple, built by Rajaraja Chola I around 1010 AD, is one of the three Great Living Chola Temples on the UNESCO list; the Saraswathi Mahal Library holds more than 49,000 manuscripts. The other two Chola temples — at Darasuram near Kumbakonam and at Gangaikonda Cholapuram — make good day trips.

The whole temple is granite. Its main tower rises 216 ft, and the great Nandi, 13 ft high and 16 ft wide, is carved from a single rock.

overview.text:
Kanchipuram is known as the 'Golden City of a Thousand Temples' — and for the silk sarees that have adorned South Indian brides for generations. Cholas, Pallavas and Vijayanagar kings ruled here, and the Palar river flows along the city's west side.

The Pallava-era Kailasanathar Temple, built around 700 CE, and the vast Ekambareswarar Temple, with an 11-storey tower, are the two sights not to miss.

overview.text:
The Pallava king Narasimhavarman II built the Kailasanathar Temple around 700 CE. It holds some of the first murals in Tamil Nadu, and inscriptions in early scripts cover its walls.

Built of sandstone on granite foundations, it is known locally as the Sand Temple; 58 small shrines surround the main sanctum.

overview.text:
Udhagamandalam — Ooty — is the 'Queen of Hill Stations', set in the Nilgiri district and once a summer resort of the British Raj.

The toy train of the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, India's only rack railway, climbs here from Mettupalayam. In town are the 55-acre Government Botanical Garden of 1897 and Ooty Lake; around it are Doddabetta, Tamil Nadu's highest peak, the falls and lake at Pykara, Avalanche and Emerald lakes, and Ketty Valley.

overview.text:
Kodaikanal, the 'Princess of Hills', sits at about 7,000 ft. British officials and missionaries established it as a hill station in 1845.

At its heart is the star-shaped Kodai Lake of 1863, with Bryant Park on its eastern shore and Coaker's Walk on the slope nearby. Boating, cycling, horse riding and trekking are the classic pastimes, and the Kurinji flower blooms here only once in 12 years.

overview.text:
Rameswaram lies on Pamban Island, joined to the mainland by the Pamban bridges. It is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites and the closest point in India to Sri Lanka.

The Ramanathaswamy Temple, one of the twelve jyotirlingas, is famous for its long pillared corridors. Beyond town, Dhanushkodi's beach runs between the Gulf of Mannar and the Bay of Bengal, and the Dr A P J Abdul Kalam Memorial honours the town's most famous son.

Kanniyakumari is the southern tip of mainland India, where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet.

Just offshore stand the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the 133-ft Thiruvalluvar Statue. On the shore are the Gandhi Mandapam, where an urn of Gandhi's ashes was kept, and the beach where you can watch both sunrise and sunset — and, on full-moon days, the sun set as the moon rises.

guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Tamil Nadu: Month-by-Month Guide
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Tamil Nadu: October–March for Madurai, Thanjavur and the coast, March–June for Ooty and Kodaikanal, plus key festivals.

body.intro: Tamil Nadu has two seasons worth knowing: the cooler months for the plains and coast, and the summer months for the hills.

sections.heading: Temple towns and the coast (about October to March)
sections.text: Madurai and Thanjavur are best from December to February; Kanchipuram from October to February; Mamallapuram from November to February; Rameswaram from October to March; and Kanyakumari from November to March. Thanjavur's summer reaches 35–40°C, and Kanchipuram gets heavy rain in July and August.

sections.heading: Hill stations (about March to June)
sections.text: Ooty is best from March to June and Kodaikanal from April to June — exactly when the plains are hottest.

guides.title: The Great Living Chola Temples: a visitor's guide
guides.summary: Thanjavur's Big Temple, Darasuram and Gangaikonda Cholapuram — what to see at each and how to visit all three.
guides.seoTitle: Great Living Chola Temples Guide: Thanjavur & More
guides.seoDescription: Visit the three Great Living Chola Temples: Thanjavur's Brihadeeswara, Darasuram's Airavatesvara and Gangaikonda Cholapuram, with how to plan the trip.

body.intro: Three Chola temples, a thousand years old and still in worship, are listed together by UNESCO. Thanjavur makes the best base.

sections.heading: Brihadeeswara Temple, Thanjavur
sections.text: Built by Rajaraja Chola I around 1010 AD, entirely of granite, with a 216-ft tower and a 13-ft Nandi carved from one rock.

sections.heading: Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram
sections.text: Built by Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century near Kumbakonam. Find the seven 'singing steps', each a musical note.

sections.heading: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
sections.text: The Chola capital for over 250 years, in Ariyalur district, with a 55 m temple tower. It was named for Rajendra I, 'the one who conquered the Ganges'.

sections.heading: Planning
sections.text: Stay in Thanjavur, about 61 km from Tiruchirappalli airport, and see the other two temples on a day trip. December to February is the most comfortable season.

checklist: Start early to avoid the heat

guides.seoDescription: Plan the Nilgiri Mountain Railway toy train: 46 km from Mettupalayam to Ooty, about 5 hours up, India's only rack railway and a UNESCO site.

body.intro: The toy train is the most memorable way to reach Ooty. Here's what to know before you book.

sections.heading: The route
sections.text: The line runs 46 km from Mettupalayam to Ooty, passing Coonoor. The climb takes nearly 5 hours; coming down takes about 4.

sections.heading: Why it's special
sections.text: It is India's only operational rack railway, and since 2005 part of the Mountain Railways of India World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: Getting to Mettupalayam
sections.text: Coimbatore — with an airport about 88 km from Ooty and a railway station — is the gateway to the foothills.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text: Ooty is best from March to June.

items.title: Best time

sections.heading: What to see
sections.text: The 14 towers, 45–50 metres tall; the thousand-pillared hall with its musical pillars; the sacred tank; and the corridor murals of the Thiruvilaiyadal puranam.

sections.heading: Festivals
sections.text: The Chithirai Brahmotsavam re-enacts the divine wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar. Navarathri falls in September–October, and in January–February the deities are floated on the Teppakulam.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: The temple was devastated in 1310 and restored in the 14th century.

guides.title: Kanyakumari guide: sunrise, the rock memorial and the southern tip
guides.summary: How to plan a visit to India's southern tip: the Vivekananda Rock, the Thiruvalluvar Statue, sunrise and sunset, and getting there.
guides.seoTitle: Kanyakumari Guide: Vivekananda Rock, Sunrise & Tips
guides.seoDescription: Plan Kanyakumari: the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and Thiruvalluvar Statue, sunrise and sunset from the beach, the Gandhi Mandapam and how to get there.

body.intro: Kanyakumari is where three seas meet at the tip of India. A day here is enough for the main sights — but stay for sunset and sunrise.

sections.heading: Three seas
sections.text: The Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet here, at the southern tip of mainland India.

sections.heading: The offshore memorials
sections.text: The Vivekananda Rock Memorial (1970) stands on a rock about 500 m from shore; beside it, the 133-ft Thiruvalluvar Statue (2000) represents the 133 chapters of the Tirukkural. Visitors can climb only to the statue's feet.

sections.heading: Sunrise, sunset and moonrise
sections.text: You can watch both sunrise and sunset from the beach. On full-moon days, the sun sets as the moon rises; on Chithra Pournami they face each other across the horizon.

sections.heading: Getting there and when
sections.text: Thiruvananthapuram airport is 76 km away and Nagercoil Junction 17 km. November to March is cool and pleasant.

checklist: Be on the beach before sunrise
